reviewPolicy.basis: Engine constants that change computed state but do not appear in decisionBasis must be reread at least every 180 days. The interval is a governance cadence, not a physiology claim.

readMe: The numbers that change a decision without belonging to any rule.
`session-rules.json` holds every threshold the session decision engine
applies, and each one is owned by a rule that declares what it cuts and
what it rests on. These are the other kind: constants inside the state
computation that no rule owns, that appear in no `decisionBasis`, and that
the caller therefore never sees — and that change what the engine decides
all the same. A detraining flag, a divisor under an HRV reading, and the
age at which a reading stops describing today are all of that kind.
They lived as bare literals in three source files until 2026-08-08. Moving
them here does not make them better evidenced; it makes the absence of
evidence visible in the same shape as everywhere else. Every one of them
is `internal_composite` with no sources, and that is the honest reading,
not an oversight to be filled in later with something plausible.
The engines read their values from this file, the same arrangement as the
rule library: editing a `value` here changes what Evidra computes. The
join is guarded in both directions by `assertParametersMatch` — a key the
engine reads that nothing here declares fails at load, and so does a
parameter nobody applies.
1.2.0, on 2026-08-09: the remaining Phase C constants moved in at their
existing values: ATL/CTL time constants, TSB bands, recovery-score weights,
readiness penalties, phase multipliers and the return ramp. The load-zone
labels remain code because the labels do not change a computation; the
numeric bands that choose them are governed here.
1.1.0, on 2026-08-09: EVD-P-001 and EVD-P-002 left. The detraining pair
gated EVD-R-007 — they decided whether that rule fired at all — so holding
them here put the trigger a tier below the rule and kept it out of the
decisionBasis the rule does reach. They are now that rule's own thresholds
in session-rules.json, at the same values. Nothing here is retired for being
wrong; this one moved because it turned out to belong to a rule.

parameters.title: HRV reference used when the athlete has no baseline of their own
parameters.definition: The divisor in the HRV recovery signal: signal = clamp(hrv / baseline x 100). A reading equal to the baseline scores 100.
parameters.appliedIn: calculateRecoveryScore, and so in recovery, readiness, and every readiness threshold the rule library cuts.
limitations: 52 has no stated origin in this repo and no citation behind it.

HRV varies by measurement method, time of day and individual by more than the differences this number is being used to detect, so a fixed divisor makes one athlete's normal night look like another's bad one. It is a fallback, and a per-athlete baseline supplied by the caller supersedes it.
It sits underneath a readiness score that rules then cut at 40, 60 and 75, so an error here moves those cut points without any of them changing.

parameters.title: Resting heart rate reference used when the athlete has no baseline of their own
parameters.definition: The reference in the resting-heart-rate signal: signal = clamp(100 - max(0, restingHr - baseline) x 5). At or below the baseline the signal is 100; every beat above costs 5 points.
parameters.appliedIn: calculateRecoveryScore, and so in recovery and readiness.
limitations: 57 has no stated origin in this repo and no citation behind it.
The penalty slope of 5 points per beat is a separate ungoverned literal in the same expression, and it decides how much this baseline matters.

parameters.title: Assumed weekly training load when the athlete's history is too short for their own
parameters.definition: Stands in for observed chronic weekly load while the 28-day window is too thin to supply one, and so sits in the denominator of the crude acute:chronic ratio.
parameters.appliedIn: calculateTrainingLoad. The decision chain supersedes the crude ratio with the impulse-response one once history has converged, so this reaches a decision only on short histories — which is exactly when it is least testable.
limitations: 360 has no stated origin in this repo and no citation behind it.
A ratio measured against an assumed target is already reported to the caller as provisional in `limits`; that sentence is the only place this number is visible from outside.

parameters.title: How old a sleep reading may be
parameters.definition: A reading older than this is dropped rather than used, and the signal is reported in signalCoverage.recovery.missing instead.
limitations: 3 is our own choice with no citation behind it.
It decides which side of the missing/usable line a sparse wearer's night falls on, so it moves confidence and — through the recovery weights — readiness.

parameters.title: How old an HRV or stress reading may be
parameters.definition: A reading older than this is dropped rather than used, and the signal is reported in signalCoverage.recovery.missing instead.
limitations: 7 is our own choice with no citation behind it.
A week-old HRV reading is admitted at full weight (0.35) rather than discounted by age, so this is a cliff rather than a decay.

parameters.title: How old a resting heart rate reading may be
parameters.definition: A reading older than this is dropped rather than used, and the signal is reported in signalCoverage.recovery.missing instead.
limitations: 14 is our own choice with no citation behind it. It is the longest window here, on the reasoning that resting heart rate moves more slowly than the other three — reasoning, not measurement.

parameters.title: How old a vendor composite score may be
parameters.definition: A composite older than this is dropped rather than used. Shorter than the raw signals because these scores are the vendor's statement about a particular day rather than a measurement that ages.
limitations: 2 is our own choice with no citation behind it.

These composites carry the heaviest weights in the recovery score (0.4, 0.3 and 0.25), so this window decides whether recovery is scored mostly by the vendor or mostly by us — and, where no raw signal is present at all, whether it is scored at all.

parameters.title: Chronic training load time constant
parameters.definition: The denominator in the CTL exponentially weighted moving average.
limitations: 42 is the conventional Banister-style chronic-load constant, but this repo has not attached a verified source to the value.

parameters.title: Acute training load time constant
parameters.definition: The denominator in the ATL exponentially weighted moving average.
limitations: 7 is the conventional acute-load constant, but this repo has not attached a verified source to the value.

parameters.title: Minimum TSB for the fresh zone
parameters.definition: A TSB at or above this value is labelled fresh.
limitations: 5 is an internal label boundary; it does not drive a session rule while detraining and ACWR govern decisions.

parameters.title: Minimum TSB for the neutral zone
parameters.definition: A TSB below fresh and at or above this value is labelled neutral.
limitations: -10 is an internal label boundary and is not a published readiness threshold.

parameters.title: Minimum TSB for the productive zone
parameters.definition: A TSB below neutral and at or above this value is labelled productive; lower values are labelled overreaching.
limitations: -30 is an internal label boundary and should not be described as a validated injury-risk cut point.

parameters.title: Required fraction of CTL history before a zone is trusted
parameters.definition: The CTL curve reports a normal zone only after history covers this fraction of the CTL time constant.
limitations: 0.5 is an internal convergence guard, not an empirical claim about exactly when the curve is reliable.

parameters.title: Acute training-load lookback
parameters.definition: The lookback used for semantic 7-day training load and the numerator of the crude ACWR.
limitations: 7 is the same acute convention used by ATL, but this crude ratio is a fallback and not the impulse-response curve.

parameters.title: Chronic training-load lookback
parameters.definition: The lookback used for semantic 28-day training load and the denominator of the crude ACWR.
limitations: 28 is an internal four-week approximation and is superseded by the impulse-response load curve when enough history exists.

parameters.title: Required fraction of semantic chronic history
parameters.definition: The crude ACWR is marked as having sufficient history only after this fraction of the chronic window is covered.
limitations: 0.5 is an internal guard against thin histories looking precise.

parameters.title: Muscle fatigue lookback
parameters.definition: Completed sessions inside this window can contribute to muscle fatigue.
limitations: 7 is an internal window; missing loads inside it are skipped and reported rather than estimated.

parameters.title: Minimum decay factor for a session in the muscle fatigue window
parameters.definition: A recent session's muscle-fatigue contribution decays no lower than this while still inside the window.
limitations: 0.15 is an internal decay floor with no source attached.

parameters.title: Days over which muscle fatigue linearly decays
parameters.definition: The denominator in 1 - ageDays / value for muscle-fatigue decay.
limitations: 5 is an internal decay slope and should not be read as a recovery half-life.

parameters.title: Sleep duration that scores 100 before blending
parameters.definition: Sleep duration is scaled as duration / value x 100 before being blended with sleep quality.
limitations: 8 is an internal normalization point; the rule does not personalize sleep need.

parameters.title: Sleep duration weight inside sleep score
parameters.definition: Weight of sleep duration when sleep duration and quality are both present.
limitations: 0.45 is an internal blend weight and is renormalized when sleep quality is absent.

parameters.title: Sleep quality weight inside sleep score
parameters.definition: Weight of sleep quality when sleep duration and quality are both present.
limitations: 0.55 is an internal blend weight and is renormalized when sleep duration is absent.

parameters.title: Sleep score weight in recovery
parameters.definition: Weight of the sleep score in recovery when all raw signals are present.
limitations: 0.35 is an internal blend weight and is renormalized over present signals.

parameters.title: HRV score weight in recovery
parameters.definition: Weight of HRV in recovery when all raw signals are present.
limitations: 0.35 is an internal blend weight; a fixed HRV baseline already has its own limitations.

parameters.title: Resting heart rate score weight in recovery
parameters.definition: Weight of resting heart rate in recovery when all raw signals are present.
limitations: 0.2 is an internal blend weight and is renormalized over present signals.

parameters.title: Stress score weight in recovery
parameters.definition: Weight of stress in recovery when all raw signals are present.
limitations: 0.1 is an internal blend weight and assumes the supplied stress score is already on a 0-100 scale.

parameters.title: Vendor readiness weight in recovery
parameters.definition: Weight of a vendor readiness composite in recovery.
limitations: 0.4 is our trust policy for vendor composites, not the vendor's own confidence.

parameters.title: Body Battery weight in recovery
parameters.definition: Weight of a Body Battery-style vendor composite in recovery.
limitations: 0.3 is our trust policy for vendor composites, not a published weighting.

parameters.title: Recovery time weight in recovery
parameters.definition: Weight of vendor recovery-time remaining after it is inverted into a recovery score.
limitations: 0.25 is our trust policy for this vendor composite, not a published weighting.

parameters.title: Recovery time that scores as fully depleted
parameters.definition: A vendor recovery-time reading at or above this value maps to a score of 0.
limitations: 1440 is a one-day cap chosen by us; it compresses all longer recovery-time readings to the same score.

parameters.title: Stress score maximum before inversion
parameters.definition: Stress contributes as this value minus the supplied stress score.
limitations: 100 assumes normalized stress scores; a source with a different scale must normalize before reaching the engine.

parameters.title: Resting heart rate penalty above baseline
parameters.definition: Each bpm above baseline subtracts this many points before the resting-HR signal is blended into recovery.
limitations: 5 is an internal slope; it determines how much the fallback resting-HR baseline matters.

parameters.title: ACWR level where readiness penalty starts
parameters.definition: Readiness loses points only for ACWR above this value.
limitations: 1.2 is an internal penalty start below the decision rule's 1.4 ACWR threshold.

parameters.title: Readiness penalty per ACWR point above start
parameters.definition: The multiplier applied to ACWR above acwrPenaltyStart when reducing readiness.
limitations: 22 is an internal coefficient with no independent validation.

parameters.title: Readiness penalty per muscle-fatigue point
parameters.definition: The multiplier applied to max muscle fatigue when reducing readiness.
limitations: 0.22 is an internal coefficient; it depends on the muscle fatigue score's own internal decay.

parameters.title: Default weekday availability when the user gives none
parameters.definition: The plan generator uses this cap when no weekday availability preference exists.
limitations: 30 is a planning default and can silently shape a plan when the caller supplies no schedule.

parameters.title: Long-session cap relative to weekday availability
parameters.definition: Long-session availability is weekday availability multiplied by this value.
limitations: 1.6 is an internal scheduling ratio, not a claim about ideal long-session duration.

parameters.title: Minimum planned session duration
parameters.definition: Generated sessions are not shortened below this duration.
limitations: 15 is an internal floor and may still be too much for some injury or illness contexts.

parameters.title: Base phase load multiplier
parameters.definition: The load multiplier for base weeks.
limitations: 1.0 anchors the template's own base minutes rather than an external load prescription.

parameters.title: Build phase load multiplier
parameters.definition: The load multiplier for build weeks.
limitations: 1.1 is an internal progression step and is not individualized.

parameters.title: Peak phase load multiplier
parameters.definition: The load multiplier for peak weeks.
limitations: 1.2 is an internal progression step and is not individualized.

parameters.title: Deload phase load multiplier
parameters.definition: The load multiplier for scheduled deload weeks.
limitations: 0.65 is an internal deload convention and is separate from ad hoc deload changes.

parameters.title: Return-to-training weekly load ramp
parameters.definition: Weekly load multipliers used for the first weeks of a generated plan after detraining.
limitations: The sequence is an internal ramp; it is governed but not evidence-based.

parameters.title: Long-session cap when availability is changed
parameters.definition: Previewing a reduced availability change sets long-session minutes to weekday minutes multiplied by this value.
limitations: 1.6 mirrors the generator's long-session cap but is governed separately because a different module applies it.

parameters.title: Minimum session duration during plan changes
parameters.definition: Availability cuts and deload changes do not shorten a session below this duration.
limitations: 15 is an internal floor and can keep a changed session longer than a user's acute situation allows.

parameters.title: Ad hoc deload change multiplier
parameters.definition: Previewing a deload_week change multiplies the week load and session durations by this value.
limitations: 0.6 is an internal deload-change factor and differs from the generated-plan deload phase multiplier of 0.65.
